Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the run-chase as the umpires make their way into the middle followed by the players of Bangladesh who could be seen positioning themselves to their respective field positions. David Warner and Travis Head are the two openers for Australia,  while Taskin Ahmed will bowl the first over.
... RUN CHASE...

Bowling from the Aussies was toothless in thefirst Powerplay but they managed to keep things under control with effective bowling right at the end. Adam Zampa was brilliant with the ball once again as he scalped a couple giving away 32 in his 10. Sean Abbott took a couple as well but was a bit expensive today, while Marcus Stoinis chipped in with a wicket as well. Marnus Labuschagne was a live wire in the field as he took a couple of catches and inflicted a couple of run-outs on his own being the difference maker as he got rid of Najmul Hossain Shanto and Mahmudullah when both of them looked like switching up a gear or two with committed fielding efforts. The target looks a decent one but the track would only get better to bat on as the day progresses. Will Australia be able to chase this down or do we have an upset on the cards? Let's find out in a while with the run-chase.

Marnus Labuschagne is down for a quick chat. He says the opposition scored really well, especially from the top surpassing the 300-run mark. Goes on to add that his secret of doing good in the field is working on the on-field awareness and moving the body into positions to field good. He also mentions they have to start well so that they can chase the score easily.

After being put in to bat first Bangladesh started a bit watchfully but capitalized fairly in the last few overs of the first powerplay scoring 62 off the first 10 overs. The first wicket fell on 76 as Tanzid Hasan edged one back to Sean Abbott off his bowling. Najmul Hossain Shanto walked in next and played well alongside Litton Das before Das lofted one down the throat of Marnus Labuschagne on an individual score of 36. The arrival of Towhid Hridoy boosted the strike rate even more and the duo of Najmul Hossain Shanto and Towhid Hridoy added 64 runs together for the 4th wicket partnership. Mahmudullah was brilliant while he stayed but an unlucky dismissal for him in the form of a run-out cut short his innings that looked promising as he was dismissed on 32 of 28 deliveries. Wickets kept falling but the strike rate was maintained well by the Bangladesh batters. Towhid Hridoy was the top scorer for them as he scored 74 runs. Everybody got starts but failed to capitalize with a big one. Mehidy Hasan played a brilliant cameo of 29 runs right at the end to add to the total.
A solid batting performance from Bangladeshi batters and Towhid Hridoy in particular helps Bangladesh manage to score 306 for the loss of 8 wickets in their quota of 50 overs.

Should have been another run out to close proceedings but Marnus Labuschagne has made a mess of it! Sean Abbott serves another slower short ball over the stumps. Taskin Ahmed is way too early in the shot and misses, getting hit on the body. The ball drops in front of the bowler and the batters try to hustle through for the single. Sean Abbott picks up the ball and throws it back to Marnus Labuschagne at the bowler's end who gets quickly behind the stumps but is unable to collect the ball cleanly and Taskin gets through for a leg bye. Bangladesh finish with 306/8!

Commentary.Commentary: Done and dusted with the pre-match formalities and it is now time to get the play underway. The umpires are out in the middle and so are the players of Australia. Tanzid Hasan and Litton Das will open the innings for Bangladesh. Josh Hazlewood has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. A couple of slips in place, let's go...

We are just a few minutes away from the start of the game but first, the two sets of players along with their mascots line up for the national anthems. It will be the national anthem of Bangladesh first followed by Australia's national anthem.

Bangladesh's stand-in captain Najmul Hossain Shanto says he would have liked to bat first anyway. Adds that they are determined to win this match and they are pretty much sure they will win the match. Informs that they have a few changes to their side with Mahedi Hasan, Mustafizur Rahman and Nasum Ahmed playing on behalf of Shakib Al Hasan, Shoriful Islam and Tanzim Hasan Sakib. Ends by saying that they are aware of the permutations regarding the Champions Trophy place.

Australia's skipper, Pat Cummins says they would like to bowl first as it looks like a good track but it might do a bit in the morning. Adds that they have made two changes as Steven Smith is back and Sean Abbott is in as well with Glenn Maxwell and Mitchell Starc being rested. Mentions that he will be hoping to restrict the opponents early on and do well with the chase as well. Says that he doesn't think they have played their best cricket as a unit so far but would be hoping to do that today.
